Set Up Your Family Scam Defense Plan in 30 Minutes

Do these five things first. The rest of the workbook gives you deeper scripts, printables, and recovery pages.

Choose the code word

Pick a private phrase that is not a pet, birthday, address, school, or social media clue.

Save trusted contact numbers

Use numbers you already trust: family, bank, local non-emergency line, and account providers.

Teach the 60-second rule

Everyone learns one response: stop, verify, call directly, refuse pressure, document, report.

Set payment rules

No urgent money, gift cards, crypto, wires, or payment-app transfers without outside verification.

Print emergency pages

Start with the code-word card, emergency contacts, fake text checklist, and incident log.

First family agreement: nobody gets in trouble for asking for help. Scammers rely on shame and silence; this plan does not.
Scam Pattern Dashboard

The Modern Scam Pattern

Most scams are not won by technology. They are won by pressure. If you can see the pattern, you can interrupt it.

1
Surprise contact
2
Emotional trigger
3
Urgency
4
Isolation
5
Payment or access
6
Shame or secrecy

What it feels like

A problem appears out of nowhere. The message sounds personal. The sender wants action before you can think.

What breaks it

Leave the conversation, verify through a trusted route, and involve a real person before money or access moves.

Threat Map

AI Scam Types in 2026

Use this page to name the situation quickly. The first safe response is almost always outside the message.

TypeWhat it looks likeFirst safe response
Voice-clone emergency callA loved one sounds panicked or someone claims to speak for them.Ask for the code word, hang up, call the known number.
Deepfake impersonationA video, image, or audio clip is used as proof.Treat media as a prompt to verify, not as proof.
Fake bank textAccount locked, suspicious charge, or urgent login link.Open the official app or call the number on the card.
Fake toll/government messageFine, court, jury duty, benefit, tax, or toll threat.Use the official public site or known agency number.
Fake delivery alertMissed package or small redelivery fee.Check the carrier app/site you choose yourself.
Romance/investment groomingAffection or friendship leads to money or investment pressure.Talk to one trusted person before sending funds.
Fake job offerCheck, equipment, training fee, or identity forms appear early.Verify company through official channels first.
Business invoice scamVendor bank change or urgent invoice exception.Known-number callback plus second approver.
Fake support agentThey contact you first and ask for codes or remote access.End contact and open official support yourself.
Core Rule

The 60-Second Rule

One calm minute can stop a rushed payment, exposed login, or bad link.

STOP
VERIFY
CALL DIRECTLY
REFUSE PRESSURE
DOCUMENT
REPORT

What to say

“I verify urgent requests first.”
“I’m calling back using the number I already have.”

What not to do

Do not click the link, read a code, install remote access, send a test payment, or keep it secret.

Involve someone when

Money, login codes, identity information, account access, secrecy, threats, or romance/investment pressure appears.

Family standard: a real emergency can survive a callback. A scam usually cannot.
Decision Tool

Scam Decision Tree

Unexpected call, text, email, DM, invoice, support chat, or QR code?
Are they asking for money, codes, account access, personal information, or remote access?
YES →
Stop. Do not pay, click, approve, or share.
Did they create urgency, fear, secrecy, romance, profit pressure, or authority pressure?
YES →
Leave the conversation. Verify through a route you choose.
Did they send a link or contact you unexpectedly?
YES →
Do not use their link. Open the official app/site yourself.
Final action: stop, verify, document, report if suspicious, and warn family or business contacts if needed.

Text Safety Rule

Never Verify Through the Message That Scared You

Fake texts work because they arrive during normal life: a bank alert, delivery issue, toll fee, payment app problem, or marketplace message.

Safe-link rule

Do not use unexpected links. Type the official site yourself or open the official app.

Official-app rule

If the alert is real, it should appear when you open the app or contact the provider directly.

Screenshot/save rule

Save the message before deleting or reporting it, especially if money or account access was involved.

Older Parent Protection

Grandparent Protection Plan

The goal is dignity plus backup. The rule is not “you cannot decide.” The rule is “nobody sends urgent money alone.”

No-shame agreement

If something feels suspicious or embarrassing, call us anyway. We will solve the problem first and discuss details calmly.

Payment pause rule

No gift cards, cash pickup, crypto, wires, or payment apps for emergency requests until two trusted people verify.

Conversation Guide

How to Talk About Scams Without Making Someone Feel Small

Opening: “I want us to have a family plan because these scams are designed to pressure careful people.”
Why this matters: “The plan is not about taking over. It gives everyone a way to pause before money moves.”
Shared rule: “If a request is urgent, secret, or about payment, we call one of these numbers first.”
What to print: “Let’s put the contact sheet near the phone and keep one in your wallet.”
If something happens: “Call me before you feel embarrassed. The sooner we know, the more options we have.”
Avoid: lectures, blame, threats to take devices away, or jokes about age. Shame helps scammers.

Business Safety

Small Business Payment Safety

For contractors, side hustlers, churches, small businesses, and local service teams. Payment changes deserve friction.

Invoice

Confirm the work, amount, and vendor before release.

Bank change

Call a known number already on file, not the email signature.

Boss request

Urgent gift cards or unusual transfers require second approval.

Overpayment

Do not refund to a different method until payment is final.

Support

Never give codes or remote access to surprise support contacts.

Documents

Verify unexpected signature links before opening.
